In my 30's I started experimenting with my diet to lower my cholesterol level. It was either that or consider medication, my doctor said. I also got engaged to a vegetarian, so I had some guidance to start. As I started cutting out eggs and pork and beef, I realized I didn't miss them that much. I lost weight and felt better, but didn't label myself a vegetarian. Then I dropped turkey and chicken later on, and didn't miss that either. This progression took about 5 years.

I figured out that most of my eating habits were cultural. Everyone is this way. My dad grew up on a farm in Iowa, and gave me never-ending loads of crap for having soy milk in my fridge, and avoiding meat in restaurants. Well guess what, 10 years later and a cancer scare later, he is a vegetarian too. Same thing happened to my grandfather. Lifelong meat eater, then has a heart problem and is king of oatmeal and vegetables.
